title: 2015 AMC 12A Problem 7
statement: Two right circular cylinders have the same volume. The radius of the second cylinder is \(10\%\) more than the radius of the first. What is the relationship between the heights of the two cylinders?

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: The second height is \(10\%\) less than the first.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: The first height is \(10\%\) more than the second.

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: The second height is \(21\%\) less than the first.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
The first height is \(21\%\) more than the
second.

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: The second height is \(80\%\) of the first.

solutions.text:
Let \(r,h\) and \(R,H\) be the radii and heights of the first and second cylinders. The volumes are equal, so \(\pi r^2 h = \pi R^2 H,\) and \(R = 1.1r.\)

Then \(\pi r^2 h = \pi(1.1r)^2 H\) \(= \pi(1.21 r^2) H.\) Dividing by \(\pi r^2\) yields \(h = 1.21H,\) so the first height is \(21\%\) more than the second.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Equal volumes give \(\pi r^2 h = \pi R^2 H\) with \(R = 1.1r\)
Divide by \(\pi r^2\) to compare \(h\) and \(H;\) note \(1.1^2 = 1.21\)
